title: 十二生肖 · 分级读物 (HSK 1-4)
source_material: 十二生肖 (The Chinese Zodiac / The Great Race) — folk tale, retold

outline.title: 玉帝的比赛
outline.summary: The Jade Emperor decides to pick twelve animals to guard the years and give each a place in order. He announces a race: all the animals must cross a wide, fast river to reach his palace, and the first twelve to arrive will each get a year named after them. The animals are excited and start preparing.
outline.recap: The Jade Emperor decides to choose twelve animals, one to be master of each year, and announces a race — all the animals must cross a wide river to his home, and the first twelve to arrive will each be given a year; the animals grow excited and start preparing.

outline.title: 猫和老鼠
outline.summary: The cat and the rat are close friends, both small and poor swimmers. They worry about the river. They agree to get up early and ride across on the back of the kind, strong ox, who swims well and agrees to carry them.
outline.recap: The cat and rat are close friends but both are small and cannot swim, and they fear the wide, deep river; the cat suggests riding across on the big, strong, kind ox, who agrees to carry them, so they plan to rise very early and find the ox together.

outline.title: 老鼠的坏主意
outline.summary: On race morning the ox carries the cat and rat into the river. Midway, the rat, wanting first place for itself, has a bad idea: it pushes the sleeping cat off the ox into the water. The cat falls in, barely struggles back to shore, and misses the race — and from then on fears water and hates rats.
outline.recap: On race morning the ox carries the sleeping cat and the rat across; wanting first place for itself, the rat shoves the sleeping cat off the ox into the river, and the cat barely swims back to shore soaked, misses the race, and from that day fears water and dislikes the rat.

outline.title: 第一名和第二名
outline.summary: As the ox reaches the far bank far ahead of everyone, the rat leaps from its head and dashes to the Jade Emperor first. The rat is named first, the ox second. The honest ox is surprised at being tricked but is not angry.
outline.recap: As the ox nears the far bank in the lead, the rat—riding secretly on its head—leaps off and races to the Jade Emperor first, taking first place; the honest ox arrives second and, realizing it was tricked, is not angry, and the Emperor notes that being fast is not everything—cleverness and effort matter too.

outline.title: 老虎和兔子
outline.summary: The tiger, powerful but fighting the strong current, drags itself ashore third, exhausted. The rabbit crosses by hopping from stone to stone and onto a floating log, nearly falling in, and arrives fourth.
outline.recap: The tiger, though strong and fast, is pushed by the fierce current and arrives third, collapsing exhausted on the bank; the clever little rabbit crosses by hopping from stone to stone, nearly falls in near the shore, but jumps onto a floating tree and reaches the far side fourth—both glad to be among the first twelve.

outline.title: 龙为什么第五
outline.summary: The dragon could fly and should have been first, but explains it stopped to make rain for a village whose fields were dry, and on the way blew the rabbit's log safely to shore. The Emperor, moved by its kindness, names the dragon fifth.
outline.recap: The dragon, who can fly and should have been first, arrives fifth; it explains it stopped to bring rain to farmers whose land had dried out, then pushed the rabbit's floating tree to shore to save it. Moved by the dragon's kindness, the Jade Emperor gladly names it fifth.

outline.title: 马和蛇
outline.summary: The horse gallops up near the front, but the snake had secretly wrapped itself on the horse's leg. Just before the finish the snake suddenly shows itself; the startled horse jumps back, and so the snake takes sixth place and the horse seventh.
outline.recap: The horse, fast and a strong swimmer, is nearly sixth, but a snake had ridden hidden on its leg; just before shore the snake darts out ahead, and the startled horse jumps back—so the snake takes sixth and the horse seventh; the horse is a little unhappy but accepts the Emperor's word that whoever arrives first ranks first.

outline.title: 羊、猴子和鸡
outline.summary: The goat, the monkey and the rooster cross together by working as a team: the rooster finds a raft, the goat and monkey clear the weeds and paddle. Pleased by their cooperation, the Emperor names the goat eighth, the monkey ninth and the rooster tenth.
outline.recap: The goat, monkey and rooster cross together as a team: the rooster spots a small boat, the monkey clears away the water weeds, the goat pushes the boat forward, and the rooster steers; pleased by their cooperation, the Jade Emperor names the goat eighth, the monkey ninth and the rooster tenth.

outline.title: 狗和猪
outline.summary: The dog is the best swimmer of all but stopped to play and wash in the cool water, arriving eleventh. The pig grew hungry on the way, ate and then slept, and arrives last, twelfth. Now all twelve places are filled.
outline.recap: The dog, the best swimmer of all, wastes time happily playing and bathing in the clean water and arrives eleventh; the pig gets hungry on the way, eats its fill and falls asleep, waking late to arrive last, twelfth—so all twelve animals have now finished and the Jade Emperor's race is over.

outline.title: 猫来晚了
outline.summary: The cat finally makes it ashore, but the race is over and all twelve years are taken — there is no place for it. Seeing the rat celebrating, the cat understands it was betrayed. From that day cats chase rats and keep away from water. The chapter closes by listing the twelve zodiac animals in order and explaining why the cat is not among them.
outline.recap: The cat finally reaches shore too late—all twelve places are taken—and, seeing the rat celebrating, realizes the rat betrayed it; from then on cats chase rats and avoid water. The twelve chosen animals become today's zodiac (rat, ox, tiger, rabbit, dragon, snake, horse, goat, monkey, rooster, dog, pig), and that is why the cat is not among them.
